name: Formal Methods for Security
description: Formal verification, proofs, and verified implementations of security-critical systems and protocols.
narrative: Early USENIX Security work used formal methods to find bugs: HeapHopper (2018) brought bounded model checking to heap allocators and DIZK (2018) built zero-knowledge proof infrastructure. A shift to verified-by-construction systems followed with VRASED (2019) and EverParse (2019).

milestones.title: HeapHopper: Bringing Bounded Model Checking to Heap Implementation Security
VRASED: A Verified Hardware/Software Co-Design for Remote Attestation

A Spectral Analysis of Noise: A Comprehensive, Automated, Formal Analysis of Diffie-Hellman Protocols
Poseidon: A New Hash Function for Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems
Formally Verified Memory Protection for a Commodity Multiprocessor Hypervisor
Speculation at Fault: Modeling and Testing Microarchitectural Leakage of CPU Exceptions
Formal verification of the PQXDH Post-Quantum key agreement protocol for end-to-end secure messaging
